fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Paul says, "…I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned." (Galatians 2:11) To his face means Paul took it up with Cephas directly. I once avoided a hard talk for a whole week, and my mustache got tired just from the dodging.

Close to the neighborhood, but no. The Pharisees aren't mentioned anywhere in these verses. The verse says Cephas "…used to eat with the Gentiles." (Galatians 2:12) That's the habit Paul is pointing at.

Nope, anger isn't in the verse. The text says Cephas pulled back "…for fear of those in the circumcision group." (Galatians 2:12) So the reason the text gives is fear. I think he was more worried about the room than mad at anybody, and I've dodged a table or two myself.

The text never says Cephas was called anywhere. It gives a reason, and the reason is fear: he drew back "…for fear of those in the circumcision group." (Galatians 2:12) I think this was one nervous moment at a table, and we've all had those.

True, baker. The text says that "…by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray." (Galatians 2:13) Barnabas had gone up to Jerusalem with Paul (Galatians 2:1), so I think that one stings. It shows how strong the pull of a crowd can be.

Paul never says that. His question is, "…how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?" (Galatians 2:14) The trouble is pressure on the Gentiles, not hiding anything from the Jews. Hide the gospel? Friend, Paul says this one out loud in front of them all.

Nice try, baker, but that's not what Paul says. His question is about pressuring the Gentiles: "…how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?" (Galatians 2:14) The complaint is about the squeeze on them. Jerusalem comes up elsewhere, but not as the complaint here.
True, baker. Paul says, "So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus…" (Galatians 2:16) Paul counts himself in that "we," right alongside the Jews by birth he's speaking about. Nobody gets a side door.
That's Paul's answer, baker. He asks if Christ is a minister of sin, and he says, "Certainly not!" (Galatians 2:17) He doesn't pause or hedge. Just a flat no.

Paul doesn't say prophet. The verse says, "If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker." (Galatians 2:18) I'll admit prophet would be a nicer title. Rebuilding just doesn't get him there.
Moses is a big name, but he's not who Paul names here. Paul says, "…I no longer live, but Christ lives in me." (Galatians 2:20) The one living in him is Christ.
Elijah doesn't appear in this passage. Paul says, "…I no longer live, but Christ lives in me." (Galatians 2:20) Great name, and no shame in picking it.

The verse says nothing like that. Paul says the Son of God "…loved me and gave Himself up for me." (Galatians 2:20) The focus is what Christ did for him, not a teaching job. I'd say that's a gift, friend, not an assignment.
